root_idea.summary: The root prominently conveys movement away, remoteness, or disappearance; this orientation extends to the sun’s setting, the west, foreignness, and the crow named for going far. Other established branches concern edges, height, whiteness, blackness, and several specialized nouns.
root_idea.development: The lexical evidence presents these branches as historically related but not wholly predictable from one rule: distance develops into sunset and western direction, while figurative extensions yield meanings such as edge, sharpness, height, foreignness, and the crow’s name.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic feminine form غَرْبِيَّة is the inflected feminine counterpart of the adjective غَرْبِيّ and is presented under that citation form.

senses.definition: To set or pass from view, especially of the sun.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of the sun in descriptions of its setting or disappearance below the horizon.

senses.definition: Intensely black; black in an emphatic degree.
senses.usage_conditions: In غَرَابِيبُ سُودٌ, the plural adjective describes strongly black or dark formations, including the black rocks or streaks of mountains.

senses.definition: Western; of or relating to the west or the place of sunset.
senses.usage_conditions: The feminine form غَرْبِيَّة is used of a thing situated toward or exposed to the west; in the Quranic lamp parable it describes a tree associated with the setting sun.

senses.definition: A crow, a familiar black bird.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is the bird sent to demonstrate how to cover the dead.

senses.definition: The setting or disappearance of the sun.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal noun of غَرَبَ, used in temporal expressions referring to sunset.

senses.definition: The west; the direction or region opposite the east.
senses.usage_conditions: The plural and dual forms refer to multiple western points or the two extreme seasonal points of sunset; the singular may denote the western direction generally.

senses.definition: The place or time of sunset; the setting point of the sun.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in expressions locating something at the sun’s setting or referring to sunset as a temporal or spatial limit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go away, withdraw, or become distant; consequently to be absent or hidden from view.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person, animal, or thing that retires from people or disappears from sight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness; also perseverance in an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of the verbal noun, with the latter application emphasizing persistence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The eye was affected by a tumour at its inner angle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized medical use of the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be strange, obscure, or difficult to understand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially said of language, a word, or an expression that is unusual or unintelligible.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become black.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate Form I verbal branch from the setting and remoteness senses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be affected by the disease called غَرَب, said of a ewe or she-goat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The disease causes loss of hair around the nose and eyes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go or direct oneself toward the west; to go far and wide.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II usage expressing movement toward the western direction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make distant, remove, put away, or banish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes expelling a person from a country or town and causing someone or something to remain remote.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To divorce a wife.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional transitive usage distinct from ordinary removal or banishment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The bringing forth of both white and black children.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage reported with correction of the interpretation that it means only one of the two kinds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The collecting and eating of hail, snow, or hoarfrost.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form II verbal-noun usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go far into a land or country.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of dogs going far in pursuit of quarry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make the place to which something is cast or shot distant or remote.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative use concerning the destination of a thrown or shot object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To run a horse much or at the utmost rate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a horse, or of a rider driving it, when the running exceeds the usual bounds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To laugh immoderately, violently, or at length.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage can imply laughter so extreme that the teeth or tears become conspicuous.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To do or say something strange, extraordinary, or unfamiliar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of unusual speech, words, or conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come to the west.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A directional Form IV usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have a white child born to one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage concerning the child’s complexion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Whiteness of the groins next to the flank.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily coloration term, also used adjectivally of a man who has this feature.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill a skin, vessel, watering-trough, or tank.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use involving the filling of a container.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be endowed with abundance of wealth and good condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The passive form presents wealth and well-being as filling the person’s hands and soul.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For pain to become intense or violent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of pain from disease or another cause.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a foul or evil deed to be done to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction and voice vary in the reported authorities; the lexical sense concerns an evil act inflicted on a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a horse’s blaze to spread beyond the eyes, leaving the eyelid edges white.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of extensive white facial or ocular markings in a horse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become a stranger or foreigner, or to become far from one’s home or native country.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes going abroad and entering the state of estrangement called غُرْبَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come from the direction of the west.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A directional usage distinct from becoming an expatriate.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To marry someone who is not of one’s kindred.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional social usage derived from taking a spouse from outside one’s kin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To regard something as strange, extraordinary, unfamiliar, obscure, or improbable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X evaluative construction meaning to hold something to be غَرِيب.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Distance or remoteness; by extension, far-seeing when applied to an eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjectival application to an eye describes vision reaching far.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first part of a thing, especially the beginning of a horse’s run.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The edge of a thing, especially a sword or tool; hence sharpness, vehemence, or force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied figuratively to the tongue, temperament, youth, a horse, or the prowess of men.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large leather bucket; also the water-carrying beast associated with it and a day of drawing water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The bucket is typically made from bull hide and used for irrigation; the associated extensions are conventional water-drawing usages.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tears, especially their copious or vehement flow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: By figurative extension, a copious uninterrupted flow of knowledge or eloquence may be compared with tears.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tear duct or vein in the eye that flows continuously; the plural can mean the channels of tears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical use connected with uninterrupted tearing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The inner or outer angle of the eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can refer to either angle according to context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tumour or persistent bleeding pustule at the inner angle of the eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A medical specialization of the ocular sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Saliva or moisture in the mouth, and by extension the lustre, whiteness, sharpness, or edges of the teeth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural غُرُوب may denote the places where saliva collects or the sharp, shining edges of the front teeth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An arrow whose shooter or direction is unknown.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression for an arrow arriving from an unidentified person or quarter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large green thorny tree of the Hijaz, used in preparing tar for treating mange in camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may be a collective noun, with a singular marked by ة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a traditional expression, the people associated with al-gharb, understood as the west or, in alternative interpretations, Syria, warriors, Arabs, or users of the large water bucket.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a disputed interpretation of a traditional phrase rather than a single settled lexical definition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Silver; in some usages, a precious substance such as gold.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence separately records gold as a usage and also gives explanations connecting the term with silver vessels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A silver drinking cup, bowl, or similar vessel; also a cup made from the associated tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun for a vessel of the قَدَح type.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A species of tree used to make white drinking cups or bowls, generally identified with a willow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical evidence distinguishes this tree from the Hijazi tree also called غَرْب.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal usage, also appearing in descriptions of what is poured into a cup.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water falling from buckets between a well and a watering-trough, together with the surrounding mud or its altered smell.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term concerns water that soon changes in odour and may make mud around the watering place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease of sheep or goats causing hair to fall from the nose and eyes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A veterinary term distinct from the eye disease and coloration terms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A blue or grey coloration of a horse’s eye accompanied by whiteness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of equine eye colour.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The state of being a stranger or foreigner; separation from one’s home or native country.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Equivalent in usage to تَغَرُّب and اِغْتِرَاب.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pure or unmixed whiteness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate nominal branch from the sense of foreignness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sort or variety of dates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This specialized noun is distinct from the directional adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A date beverage made from crushed unripe or fresh ripe dates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reported preparation and effects vary in the lexical accounts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain red dye or colouring fluid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A superior kind of intensely black grapes associated with al-Taif.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun, distinct from the emphatic colour adjective used in the Quranic form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Applied to an old man whose hair is intensely black, does not whiten, or has been blackened with dye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet with several reported applications concerning the hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The southern constellation Corvus, the Crow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical astronomical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The black Arabs, especially people whose black complexion was inherited through their mothers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective epithet likening these people to crows.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular herb or medicinal plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plant name with detailed botanical and medicinal identifications in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A method of tightly binding a camel’s udder so that the young cannot suck; figuratively, a matter made difficult or constricted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The figurative idiom derives from the binding method.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An extremity or prominence of the haunch, hip, or croup of a horse or camel; the plural can denote the haunches themselves.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical term with several closely related descriptions of the rear body.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The whole of the back of the head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions describing the hair of that part becoming white.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bunch of the fruit of the arak tree, especially its ripe black fruit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hail, snow, or hoarfrost.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Explained through the whiteness associated with the dawn.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stranger, foreigner, or person not of one’s own people or kindred.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine and plural forms extend the same sense to women and groups.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Strange, unusual, obscure, or difficult-to-understand language or expression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A word or expression so described is opposed to فَصِيح and may be treated as a technical category of rare language.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Improbable or unfamiliar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived evaluative use of the notion of strangeness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hadith traced continuously to the Prophet but transmitted at a relevant generation by only one person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical hadith classification.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Black, in a poetic usage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence treats this as possibly a poetic substitute for غِرْبِيبَة and therefore a specialized or uncertain application.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hand-mill.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative feminine-noun use, so called because neighbours borrow it and it does not remain with its owners.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A variety of dates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agricultural noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The western side of a mountain or similar feature.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A directional noun opposed to شَارِق or the eastern side.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The withers or forepart of the hump of a camel, between the neck and hump.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural refers to the corresponding paired prominences; the term may cover the upper forepart of the hump.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave someone’s way free or open to go wherever they wish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression originating in placing a camel’s leading rope on its withers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The upper part of a wave or the highest part of anything.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from the elevated forepart of a camel’s hump.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place or thing that conceals, veils, or covers another; a hiding-place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural مَغَارِب is applied especially to the lurking-places of wild animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: White, especially white in every part or at the edges of the eyelids.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to animals, horses, and eyes with extensive white markings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The dawn of day.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Named for its whiteness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A legendary or unidentified great bird, said to go far in its flight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The phrase can also be treated as a name whose body is unknown.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Calamity or misfortune that carries someone away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use of the legendary expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The summit of a high eminence or the highest part of a tall mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An interpretation that rejects the bird meaning and treats the phrase as a topographical expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person or woman who has gone far into a country and is no longer perceived or seen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional interpretation with the feminine ending suppressed in the phrase.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Western or of the west; in later usage, specifically Maghribi or from North-West Africa.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the nisbah adjective formed from مَغْرِب and is distinct from the Quranic headword غَرْبِيّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Distant or remote.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a term, limit, or distance; the passive counterpart is also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: New or recent information from a foreign or distant land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression for news arriving from far away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: People believed to have a share or partnership of the jinn in them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A traditional interpretation explains the foreign element as causing or encouraging unlawful sexual conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One going to or toward the west.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A participial directional use.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Definition only announces the senses in following units.
The unit explicitly treats غَرْب as synonymous with مَغْرِب.
Editorial report of an unsupported lexicographical assignment.

cautions: The Quranic form غَرَابِيب is presented under the singular citation form غِرْبِيب; its Quranic occurrence is plural.
غَرْبِيَّة is an inflected feminine form and is accounted for under the adjective citation form غَرْبِيّ.

The traditional expression أَهْلُ الغَرْب has several reported interpretations, including west, Syria, warriors, Arabs, and users of the large bucket; these should not be treated as one settled definition.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The interpretation of أَهْلُ الغَرْب in lane-unit:grb:29033:g7:main remains lexically and contextually disputed; the artifact preserves the principal alternatives in a qualified conventional-expression meaning.
The poetic use of غَرِيبَة meaning black in lane-unit:grb:29043:g2:main is reported as possibly a poetic form of غِرْبِيبَة and is therefore marked as specialized and uncertain.
